title: Richard Diamond, Private Detective
paragraphs: Dick Powell stars as the quick-witted private eye Richard Diamond, whose murder cases combine hard-boiled detective plotting with humor, romance, and Diamond's habit of ending adventures at the piano.

Weekly private-detective series created/written chiefly by Blake Edwards around Dick Powell. The format deliberately combined Powell’s wisecracking tough-guy image with a recurring musical sign-off. GRH contains 106 playable items, beginning with an AFRS item dated 1949-05-01; the documented network series began 1949-04-24.

GRH documents the program through NBC original run (April 24, 1949 to December 6, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], ABC original run (January 5, 1951 to June 27, 1952) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], and CBS repeat summer run (May 31, 1953 to September 20, 1953) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|dick-powell|Dick Powell]] (performer on 94 recordings), Frank Worth (composer on 30 recordings, conductor on 30 recordings, music director on 28 recordings, and music on 22 recordings), [[person|virginia-gregg|Virginia Gregg]] (performer on 74 recordings), Blake Edwards (writer on 66 recordings, director on 10 recordings, and editor on 5 recordings), Wilms Herbert (performer on 69 recordings), Ed Begley (performer on 40 recordings), and Jaime del Valle (transcriber on 22 recordings, director on 7 recordings, and producer on 7 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), and [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).
